batch_strategy: Select matched condition and loading contrasts where measured outcomes distinguish scaffold-specific response curves, then add common-row controls and one diagnostic point near inconsistent records. All choices use the supplied packet predictions.

choices.reason: m78 at 5/1 and 100 ul starts a fixed-loading condition series. The prediction is approximately 12.26/25.88 mL; the label will connect ordinary low-ratio behavior to the measured late 50/1 regime.
m78 at 10/1 keeps sample amount and loading solvent fixed relative to the selected 5/1 point. Its predicted 23.59/43.30 mL tests the steep middle portion of the response curve.

m78 at 20/1 completes the intermediate series at the same loading. Predicted 38.41/66.15 mL, it tests whether both endpoints approach the measured late regime gradually or through a sharper transition.

m81 at 20/1 and 100 ul tests whether its ordinary measured 10/1 behavior persists under weaker eluent. Comparing this beta-ketoester with the selected m78 series can teach structural specificity beyond carbonyl counts.

m81 at 50/1 and the same loading extends that contrast. The relatively early prediction, approximately 7.25/22.25 mL, is informative whether confirmed or displaced toward the late behavior of related beta-ketoesters.

m25 at 50/1 and 100 ul explores an unmeasured weak-eluent condition for tert-butyl acetoacetate. Its predicted 19.52/49.88 mL complements the m78 and m81 contrasts and extends measured moderate-ratio behavior.
m118 at 10/1 and 50 ul tests loading dependence near a measured condition with unusually early onset and much later finish. The supplied prediction is approximately 10.96/32.92 mL.

m118 at 20/1 holds the low loading fixed while weakening the eluent. Predicted 31.15/68.89 mL, it fills the gap before the measured very late 50/1 outcome and discriminates smooth growth from a threshold.
m59 at 10/1 and 100 ul supplies an intermediate aldehyde condition between measured 5/1 and 20/1 behavior. It establishes the lower point of a matched extension to 50/1.

m59 at 50/1 keeps loading fixed relative to the selected 10/1 point. The predicted 34.76/60.75 mL and high feature-space distance make this a useful exploration of an ether-containing aldehyde response.

m38 at 20/1 and 50 ul probes a predicted strong rise to approximately 39.34/72.06 mL. Existing lower-ratio labels anchor this fused aromatic ketone, allowing a focused test of the weak-eluent transition.
m199 at 1/1 and 50 ul fills the low-ratio gap between measured pure-EA and 2/1 behavior. It anchors the sulfoxide response before the large measured changes at weaker eluent.
m199 at 5/1 and 50 ul contrasts the measured high-loading 5/1 outcome. Its predicted 27.91/53.96 mL tests whether the late response persists at one-third the sample amount.

m199 at 2/1 and 150 ul supplies the reciprocal loading contrast to the measured low-loading 2/1 point. Together with the selected low-loading 5/1 row, it separates amount sensitivity from solvent-strength sensitivity.
m101 at 10/1 and approximately 50 mg tests the intermediate response before its measured late 50/1 regime. It is the lower-loading member of a matched pair whose predictions are almost identical.

m101 at 10/1 and approximately 150 mg completes the threefold loading contrast. The pair tests whether the weak loading dependence suggested by measured 50/1 outcomes transfers to this intermediate ratio.
m174, benzyl benzoate, at 30/1 and 150 ul bridges the measured lower-loading 30/1 and higher-loading 50/1 records. It helps resolve onset and finish responses within the ester family.

m174 at 100/1 and 150 ul extends the same-loading series beyond measured 50/1 behavior. Predicted 27.01/45.52 mL, it tests extrapolation for very weak mobile phase without assuming every benzoate shares its slope.
m56 at 40/1 and 50 ul fills an intermediate-ratio gap for isobutyl benzoate. Such intermediate ratios recur in the catalog, so calibrating its predicted finish has direct distribution relevance.
m56 at 100/1 holds loading fixed relative to the selected 40/1 point. Its modest predicted 7.92/17.75 mL provides a useful contrast to the stronger predicted response of benzyl benzoate.
m84 at 20/1 and 50 ul extends measured 10/1 ethyl chlorobenzoate behavior. It anchors a matched intermediate-ratio series with the same PE loading solvent and loading volume.
m84 at 40/1 completes the fixed-loading ratio contrast. Predicted onset changes little while finish reaches approximately 20.41 mL, directly testing endpoint-specific solvent response.

m85 at 50/1 and 50 ul tests weak-eluent behavior of ethyl fluorobenzoate. Comparison with the selected ethyl chlorobenzoate points and existing methyl-benzoate labels can teach substitution and ester-environment effects.
m80 at 1/1 and 50 ul adds an ordinary diester point at a loading absent from the measured 1/1 series. It helps calibrate common early finishes while checking transfer across loading levels.
m70 at 10/1 and 150 ul supplies an ordinary aromatic-ketone control, predicted approximately 4.31/10.76 mL. It checks whether late corrections remain conditional on structural environment.
m12 at 50/1 and 50 ul extends measured moderate-ratio indene behavior. Its predicted early onset but later finish tests interval calibration for a hydrocarbon without donor or acceptor groups.

m48 at 5/1 and 50 ul tests whether the recent correction of underestimated 1/1 endpoints transfers to a neighboring condition. The compact predicted 4.67/6.32 mL interval makes this a useful common-row check.

m73 in pure EA at 100 ul fills the middle loading level near records with reversed endpoint ordering. It tests local record consistency; those unusual labels do not establish a physical retention mechanism.

m92 at 20/1 and 100 ul fills the loading level between measured low- and high-loading outcomes with different endpoints. It tests whether the intermediate point supports a consistent loading relationship.
m92 at 50/1 and 150 ul completes a missing loading corner. It tests whether finish remains late across amounts or changes preferentially at high loading, as suggested by lower-ratio observations.
m131 at 50/1 and 100 ul probes an early-onset, extended-finish diaryl-ketone prediction. It provides a structural contrast to the much later measured methoxybenzophenone response.
m114 at 10/1 and 100 ul fills the condition gap before its measured late 20/1 and 50/1 behavior. The label tests where methoxybenzophenone begins moving away from ordinary diaryl-ketone retention.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-strength responses depend strongly on scaffold and can move onset and finish differently. Some families develop steep weak-eluent transitions, while related structures retain ordinary onset or finish behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched curves across beta-ketoesters, aldehydes, benzoates, sulfoxides, and diaryl ketones can teach structure-condition interactions and prevent a global late-retention correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which selected intermediate conditions reveal smooth endpoint movement, and which locate a sharp transition specific to the scaffold?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading contrasts can be endpoint-specific and condition-dependent, but not every difference can be assigned causally to loading because repeated tuples also vary.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Targeted loading pairs and missing matrix corners test the predictor's nearly flat amount responses while distinguishing conditional sensitivity from record variability.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m199 and m101 contrasts and the intermediate m92 labels support stable loading relationships for onset, finish, or interval width?

hypotheses.content: Common early-to-moderate rows still need local endpoint calibration, including finishes that remain extended despite early onset.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controls in common retention regimes help improve overall Row accuracy and constrain how far corrections learned from rare late failures should spread.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected m80, m70, m12, and m48 conditions preserve ordinary onset and scaffold-specific finish behavior?

hypotheses.content: Some repeated recorded tuples have materially different endpoints, and some m73 records reverse V1/V2 ordering. These observations limit mechanistic interpretation and leave local consistency unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recognizing record heterogeneity avoids fitting a confident causal loading or solvent rule to inconsistent labels. A neighboring unmeasured tuple can test how broadly the unusual recorded pattern extends.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m73 middle-loading pure-EA label follow the late recorded onsets, the current model estimate, or another endpoint pattern?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes favor selective local repair. The m101 50/1 labels were similarly late at two amounts, whereas m81 and m92 sometimes finished substantially earlier than their acquisition-time predictions. The latest m81 high-loading 10/1 finish also differs from an earlier measurement at the same recorded tuple, weakening a purely causal loading explanation. Late behavior remains well supported for the sulfoxide and several carbonyl-rich scaffolds, but ordinary controls show that the correction should not spread globally. I also use the supplied SMILES to identify m174 correctly as benzyl benzoate. Reversed m73 endpoints are treated as a record-consistency issue rather than evidence of a physical late-elution mechanism.
batch_rationale: The batch combines linked experiments with direct distribution relevance. Fixed-loading m78, m81, m118, and m59 extensions locate condition-response transitions; m199, m101, and m92 contrasts test whether amount sensitivity transfers across solvent strengths and endpoints. Benzoate measurements cover intermediate and very high ratios that recur in the catalog, using structural contrasts to distinguish onset shifts from finish extension. The m131/m114 pair tests transfer within diaryl ketones. Four ordinary controls constrain common-row calibration, and one m73 point examines an inconsistent neighborhood without assuming its labels describe a physical mechanism. These labels should improve the retrained model's conditional response surfaces across the Row-distribution rather than merely emphasize the latest-eluting experiments.
